name: publicWeb_deletePasskey
description: Web member's door to HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey (E9.F7.S18): removes one of the member's passkeys by clearing the credential columns on that HC.Device row. The device row and its secret survive, so a browser removing its own passkey stays signed in. A thin wrapper that EXECs the app SP with the same arguments and returns its envelope and remaining-passkey rowset unchanged; it adds no checks of its own. Auth: the wrapped SP's HC6.ValidateAppAuth — token signed for hcapp_deletePasskey; the hasher comes from the token and the UPDATE is scoped to them.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The browser's HC.Device id (the web member session). No SQL default.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token signed for hcapp_deletePasskey (the SP that validates it). No SQL default.

parameters.name: targetDeviceId
parameters.description: The device whose passkey to remove. Passed straight through; NULL is refused by the app SP (1950).

rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey: Auth failure (ValidateAppAuth: 1220/1320 + signed-out 1220 errorType 7) returns the error detail ALONE — no envelope row before it.

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey: On a refusal after auth: { success = 0, errorCode, errorType } then the detail at index 1. 1950 missing targetDeviceId (errorType 2); 1951 passkey not found / not yours / already gone (3); 1952 unhandled (5) — on that path the envelope is { success = 0, errorMessage = ERROR_MESSAGE() } instead.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: 1950 / 1951. (Absent on the CATCH path, which emits errorMessage.)

rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey: Error detail after an ErrorEnvelope (1950, 1951, 1952).

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey: On success: the standard success envelope.

rowsets.name: Passkeys
rowsets.description: As returned by HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey: On success: the hasher's REMAINING passkey-bearing live devices, newest sign-in first — identical in shape to hcapp_listPasskeys rowset 1. May be empty.

columns.name: Label
columns.description: 'Safari on iPhone', 'Harrier Central on iPhone' — from Device.OperatingSystem / IsMobile and HC6.DevicePlatformName(DeviceData).

columns.name: IsThisDevice
columns.description: 1 when the row is the calling @deviceId.

sideEffects: EXEC HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey with the same arguments — every side effect is the wrapped SP's:

UPDATE HC.Device SET PasskeyCredentialId/PasskeyPublicKey/PasskeyCounter/PasskeyTransports = NULL, updatedAt = GETDATE() WHERE id = @targetDeviceId AND UserId = @userId AND removed = 0 AND PasskeyCredentialId IS NOT NULL (inside a transaction).
INSERT LOG.GeneralLog ('HC6.hcapp_deletePasskey', 'Passkey removed', userId, 'device=… label=… by=…') — audit trail of the revocation, in the same transaction.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 1950 (pre-flight, outside the transaction), 1951 (after ROLLBACK, so the row survives) and in the CATCH.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog ('<web>', userId NULL, deviceId) then THROW in the wrapper's CATCH, for an error the wrapped SP does not handle itself.

codeSmells.detail: @deviceId and @accessToken have no SQL default (line 21). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
